statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20% (watch), Stress 54% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high), dominant mode trend-up. NQZ26 trades 31,354.00 at 19:17:05Z, up 292.25 points or 0.94% on the 31,061.75 prior close, after a fourth new record high of 31,363.25 and holding roughly 9 points beneath it into power hour.
recommendation: Tail at 20% crosses into the watch band, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH and yellow for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Tail rises one point from the prior hour because the 31,317.25 record named an hour ago has been exceeded at 31,363.25, price now holds roughly 9 points under the extreme rather than 19, and the cash index and S&P 500 are both effectively on their own session highs with roughly half an hour to the cash close. It stays five points below the 25% block threshold because the amplifier stack is not aligned: advancing issues lead decliners only 1.04-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.09-to-1 on the Nasdaq, the Philadelphia semiconductor index is lower with most components down, the 30-year at 5.67% and crude down more than 2% conflict with the equity bid, VIX is decaying off its session high, and a material share of the advance is single-stock deal flow rather than index-level structure. Tail remains below the block threshold; the narrow evidence-based danger window is power hour into the 20:00Z cash close.
headline: Tail crosses to 20% and the watch band as NQ sets a fourth record at 31,363.25 and holds within 9 points of it, while near one-to-one breadth and a 5.67% 30-year cap the risk
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 19% on a third record extreme at 31,317.25. That extension has continued into power hour rather than stalling, which is why Tail now crosses into the watch band.

NQZ26 has printed a fourth record high of 31,363.25 and the last verified quote is 31,354.00 at 19:17:05Z, up 292.25 points or 0.94% on the 31,061.75 prior close, against a 31,059.00 open and a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,363.25. Price is holding roughly 9 points beneath the extreme, tighter than the 19-point distance an hour ago. The cash market confirms it: NASDAQ-100 is 31,113.02 at 19:26:59Z, up 305.09 points or 0.99% on a 30,807.93 prior close, about 4 points under its own 31,117.36 session high. The S&P 500 at 7,790.51 is up 0.88% and also about 4 points under its 7,794.35 high.

This is the fourth consecutive new extreme of the session, each following a retracement that failed to hold, with price pinned at the high roughly half an hour before the 20:00Z cash close. Repeated extension after failed pullbacks into the close is the pattern that most reliably precedes a path which denies meaningful mean reversion, and it is the reason the published value moves to the watch band.

What holds it five points below the block threshold is that the amplifier stack is conflicting rather than aligned, and on two counts it is weaker than the index print suggests. Breadth is the clearest. Advancing issues outnumber decliners by only 1.04-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.09-to-1 on the Nasdaq, which is close to an even split beneath a record index level. The Philadelphia semiconductor index is lower, by about 0.3% to 0.7% depending on the cut, with most of its components trading down, even though the megacap-weighted SMH is 634.10 and up 0.56%. One report notes this would be only the second occasion in 2026 on which the Nasdaq Composite gained more than 0.5% while the semiconductor index fell more than 0.5%. A record set on near one-to-one breadth with chips lagging is a narrow, megacap-led advance, not the broad alignment that produces an index-level one-way path.

The cross-asset stack conflicts in the same direction. The 10-year note yield is 5.32%, up about four basis points, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 30-year at 5.67% after a rise of roughly six basis points, reported as its highest level since 2002. Crude is sharply lower, with WTI at 88.97 dollars down 2.34% and Brent at 99.98 dollars down 2.22%. VIX is 15.61 at 19:12:01Z, up 1.96% on the day but well off its 16.38 session high, so implied volatility is decaying as price rises rather than pricing a disorderly path. The magnitude is also modest: a 0.94% day with a 405.75-point range is an orderly grind, not violent directional repricing, and the earlier 62.50-point pullback to 31,192.25 was genuine two-way trade.

The composition of the advance matters as well. Megacaps are leading, with Meta and Tesla up more than 2% and Microsoft and Nvidia up more than 1%, but a material share of the index move is idiosyncratic deal flow: PTC is up more than 30% on Schneider Electric's 22.6 billion dollar all-cash bid at 205 dollars a share, and RXO is up 21.8% on a 5.8 billion dollar C.H. Robinson agreement, against C.H. Robinson itself down 12.9%. Single-stock merger moves do not create index-level one-way structure. The yield backdrop remains identifiable: September ISM Services printed at 54.9% at 14:00Z with the Prices Index at 74.0%, its highest since July 2022, Business Activity at 56.5%, New Orders at 59.8% and Employment back in expansion at 50.1%, which has kept the long end firm even after the soft payroll print at the end of last week. The Dow has extended its gain to 51,377.51, up 0.39%, so participation has broadened somewhat through the afternoon, but the Nasdaq-100 still leads it by better than two to one.

The narrow evidence-based window is therefore power hour into the cash close, 19:00Z to 20:15Z. That is where a session already pinned at its extreme could convert into late-session continuation, and it is the only hour of the 24 modelled where the published path reaches the watch band. After the 20:00Z close index liquidity drains and the published path falls back through 19% and 15% to a 10% overnight trough.

The shared Finviz context file was read and not used. Its generatedAt is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly six days old, and its collectionStatus is partial, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness bound and cannot support current cross-asset evidence. Every level cited above was fetched independently from primary sources instead, which is why Confidence holds at 88% despite the unavailable shared feed.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 18:00Z, Claude published Tail between 3% and 19% and Stress between 46% and 71%, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green. Tail sat at 3% through the Oct 4 US evening, rose into a 12% to 15% overnight band, troughed at 6% during the European morning, and then climbed in steps through the US session, from 7% at midday to 17%, 18% and 19% as successive session highs were tested, rejected and then exceeded three times. Stress fell steadily from 71% late on Oct 4 to 46% by midday Oct 5 before firming back to 53% as the long end pressed higher. Dominant mode was normal overnight, briefly trend-down at 10:00Z, mixed through most of the US morning, and trend-up at 14:00Z and again from 17:00Z. One hour, 06:00Z on Oct 5, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The published path treats power hour into the US cash close as the one window where current evidence supports watch-band risk. Tail is 20% at 19:00Z, the only slot of the 24 that maps to WATCH and yellow, then returns to 19% across the 20:00Z close before falling through 15% and 13% as the cash session ends and liquidity drains. The overnight trough is 10% in the Tokyo and Asian mid-session hours, with Stress bottoming at 44%. Risk rebuilds gradually through the Asian and European sessions, with mode shifting to mixed at the 07:00Z European open, and the published path then tracks the Oct 6 US calendar: 14% across the 12:15Z weekly ADP and 12:30Z balance of trade block, a 17% secondary peak at 13:00Z covering Fed Williams at 13:05Z and the 13:30Z cash open, 16% through Fed Bowman at 14:45Z, and 14% into the 17:00Z 3-year note auction before easing to 13%. Every slot other than 19:00Z stays inside the low band. Forward values are conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price path has been observed.
